title: Telemetry IaC: roll-forward autorepair for Prometheus/Grafana/OTel/logship
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Create a Terraform module and associated automation that performs safe roll-forward upgrades and automated self-repair for the VPC observability stack (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry Collector, and log shipping agents). The goal is to reduce manual intervention during module upgrades and to provide deterministic health gates and fast rollback when a canary detects regression. This combines Terraform/Helm orchestration, a small controller for reconciliation checks, and synthetic health probes run from a centralized runner in the customer VPC.
acceptance_criteria: Module can perform a staged canary upgrade (1% -> 10% -> 100%) using Terraform/Helm with zero-downtime scrape continuity for Prometheus targets
Automated health gate triggers rollback if: Prometheus scrape success < 98% for canary namespace OR Grafana API returns dashboards unhealthy OR < 95% log throughput to log-ship endpoint
Reconcile controller detects drift (missing configmap/secrets/helmrelease mismatch) and can restore desired state within 5 minutes or create a ServiceNow stub for manual approval
Terraform plan/apply flow documented and integration test (ci) validates upgrade path and rollback on failure
Module exposes metrics (telemetry_module.upgrade_status, reconcile_actions_total, last_successful_canary) and these are visible in Redwood Console demo dashboard
tasks: Design: define canary percent stages, health gate thresholds, and quorum logic
Implementation: terraform module packaging with optional helm_release resource for Prometheus/Grafana/otel/shipper
Add: reconcile-controller (lightweight k8s controller) that watches HelmRelease/ConfigMaps and reports metrics
Create: synthetic probe runner job (k8s CronJob) to execute scrape, grafana-api, and log ingest smoke tests
CI: integration test harness in infra-ci that performs a fake upgrade and asserts health gates
Docs: step-by-step upgrade/runbook + terraform inputs reference + rollback procedure
Review & security: threat model review for builder runner (no secret exfil), generate input whitelist for KMS

notes: Choice rationale: Using HelmRelease + Terraform minimizes tfstate churn while keeping upgrade semantics in Terraform. Reconcile-controller is intentionally minimal: only detects and repairs a small set of known drift patterns (values.yaml mismatch, missing secret, stuck helm release).

Security: probe runner will run with a service account that has limited permissions: list/get/watch for the cluster in the observability namespace only. KMS keys used for secrets must be customer-managed for Private deployments.

Rollback plan: Terraform apply will mark canary partition. If health gate fails, automation triggers a terraform apply using previous values file (stored in git tag) and reconciler performs forced restore. Operators are paged with runbook link and an on-call playbook is documented in Confluence.
